note: Lifted semantic model, Vertex (overlay SDN) side. Home-grown, no standard vocabulary. Vertex (the VXLAN/EVPN overlay) and the DC fabric OSS touch only at the underlay binding. Concepts carry a bespoke label, synonyms, a kind, a gloss, an example, the ad-hoc reference entry bound to (ref; native-only concepts bind to a native-gap ref), relations, and instances. Carries the surface partner of the 'zone' trap (security-zone near availability-zone) and one opaque tag. ref=null marks an opaque item.

concepts.label: vtep-binding
concepts.gloss: the binding on a VTEP that maps an overlay segment (VNI) onto the underlay for local delivery
concepts.example: the binding of VNI 50201 to the underlay on VTEP leaf-3

concepts.label: overlay-segment
concepts.gloss: an overlay segment identified by a VNI: one tenant broadcast domain spanning the overlay independent of physical VLANs
concepts.example: VNI 50201 for tenant-blue across all VTEPs

concepts.label: vtep-node
concepts.gloss: a VXLAN tunnel endpoint (typically co-located on a leaf) that encapsulates and decapsulates overlay traffic

concepts.label: overlay-mtu
concepts.gloss: the MTU the overlay expects the underlay to carry so encapsulated frames are not fragmented
concepts.example: 9216-byte MTU required from the fabric for VXLAN

concepts.label: anycast-gateway
concepts.gloss: the distributed anycast gateway the overlay programs on every VTEP so a tenant's default route is local everywhere
concepts.example: anycast gateway 10.20.1.1 for VNI 50201 on all VTEPs

concepts.label: microseg-policy
concepts.gloss: a micro-segmentation policy controlling which workloads may talk within and across overlay segments - an overlay-internal object with no fabric counterpart
concepts.example: allow web->app, deny app->db for tenant-blue

concepts.label: security-zone
concepts.gloss: a security zone: a named grouping of workloads to which micro-segmentation rules attach - an overlay-internal notion of a 'zone', unrelated to any physical fault domain
concepts.example: the 'dmz' security zone grouping the tenant's internet-facing workloads
